entry.title: From SAP TechEd Berlin to Your Next Blog Post
entry.content:
Hello SAP Community!

I’m Fatemeh Zarei, and I’ve been working with the SAP Community team for over a year now, creating content and helping share stories from across the community.

During this time, I’ve had the opportunity to attend D-COM and SAP Inside Track Hamburg. Attending SAP Inside Track Hamburg gave me the opportunity to enjoy interesting sessions and connect with fellow community members. I’ve always loved events for exactly this reason: the chance to exchange ideas and get to know the people behind the technology. That experience helped me better understand SAP technology and connect with the great SAP community in Hamburg.

That’s also why I enjoy hearing people’s stories after an event. We can attend the same event and come away with completely different experiences. A session you almost skipped might become your biggest takeaway, or a quick conversation might introduce you to someone you’ll stay connected with.

So, why not share your upcoming SAP TechEd Berlin experience with the SAP Community?

You don’t need to be an experienced blogger, and you don’t need to write about everything that happened. A few highlights, useful lessons, or memorable community moments are a great place to start.

Let’s go!

Your SAP TechEd Story: 10 Questions to Get You Started

Use some of the questions below as a starting point for your blog post draft. Choose the ones that are meaningful to you, skip the others, and add anything else you’d like to share.

Who are you, and what brought you to SAP TechEd?

Introduce yourself briefly. Tell readers about your role, your interests, and whether this was your first SAP TechEd.

What were you most looking forward to, and how did the experience compare?

Perhaps you wanted to explore a particular technology, get hands-on experience, or meet fellow community members. Tell us how it went and what surprised you.

Which session stood out to you, and why?

Share what made it worth attending and your main takeaway. Include a link to the session or related resources so readers can explore further.

What technology or idea are you excited to explore further?

Whether it’s SAP Business AI, Joule, application development, integration, or something completely different, tell us what caught your attention and why.

What did you learn that you could apply in your work?

Describe a practical tip, a new approach, or an idea you’d like to try with your colleagues, customers, or projects.

Did a session or conversation change your perspective?

Tell us what you thought before and what made you see things differently. It could be a technical insight or something you learned from another person’s experience.

Who did you connect with, and what made that interaction memorable?

Maybe you met someone you previously knew only online, reconnected with a community friend, or had an unexpected conversation. Share what made that connection special and tag the people you met so they can join the conversation. If you took a picture together, consider including it, with their permission of course 🙂

What was your favorite SAP TechEd moment?

Choose one moment that captures the event for you. If you have a picture, include it and tell us the story behind it: what was happening, who you were with, and why it mattered.

What advice would you give a first-time attendee?

Share a practical tip you wish you’d known beforehand—whether it’s about choosing sessions, preparing for the event, or making time for community activities.

What comes next?

Tell us what you plan to do with what you learned. You might try a new technology, share your takeaways with colleagues, stay in touch with someone you met, or create your next SAP Community contribution.

Now It’s Your Turn! ✨

Your blog post doesn’t have to follow this exact order or answer all ten questions. Choose the ones that help you tell your story and add pictures and useful links along the way.

Before publishing, complete the Tour the SAP Community tutorial if you haven’t already, it’s required for blogging and will help you get familiar with the platform before sharing your story.

Ready to share? Create your blog post in Community Corner and add the SAP TechEd and SAP Community tags so others can find your story.

Finish by inviting readers to join the conversation. You could ask: “What was your biggest SAP TechEd takeaway?”

Most of all, write in your own voice. Your experience and perspective are what make your contribution worth reading.

I’m looking forward to reading your SAP TechEd stories and discovering the sessions, people, and moments that made the event special for you!

Have fun blogging!

The following blog post is relevant only for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Please note that Developer Extensibility is required.

 

Use Case:

At the time of writing this blog, the only available use case for BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD~CHANGE_INVOICE_TYPE is for country France. With this BAdI you can overwrite the value found in customizing activity "Determine Process Type and Invoice Attributes for Accounting Document Type".

 

Implementation:

To implement, use method "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud~change_invoice_type" in BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD (enhancement spot ES_EDOCUMENT_CLOUD). The method “change_invoice_type” receives the source data in the importing parameter “is_source_data”, "iv_source_key", "iv_source_type", "iv_edoc_type" and "iv_edoc_guid". The changing parameter “CV_INV_TYPE” allows you to change the invoice type determined by the customizing table.

Implementation Steps:

  1. Create implementation for enhancement spot ES_DOCUMENT_CLOUD.
  2. Create BAdI implementation for EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD.
  3. (Optional) Create BAdI Filter for Country and/or Generic Filter.
  4. Create implementing class for BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD, which implements the interfaces "if_badi_interfaces" and "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud".
  5. Implement method "change_invoice_type" of interface "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud" in your BAdI class.
  6. Activate your BAdI implementation.

entry.title: SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026 Release: RBPs are Changing, Here’s What to Check Before November 13, 2026
entry.content:
Why this release matters

The 2H 2026 release includes six changes to Role-Based Permissions (RBP) and the areas around it. They cover who can act as a proxy, which MDF objects are secured by default, how Learning administrators are assigned, how RBP changes are audited, what Performance Management data shows up in Story reports, and what the RBP REST APIs return.

SAP rates two of them Major (proxy and Learning). All six are valid as of 13 November 2026. Five switch on automatically, and only the Story permission is customer-configured.

 

Change

Reference

Type

Major / Minor

Enablement

Module-level proxy access control

PLA-57182

Changed

Major

Automatically on

More MDF objects secured by default

ECT-257018

Changed

Minor

Automatically on

Learning admin roles assigned through RBP

PLA-57203

Changed

Major

Automatically on

RBP change audit reports in two versions (V2)

PLA-56544

Changed

Minor

Automatically on

Hide Story report data for forms never in Inbox

PMU-27006

New

Minor

Customer configured

RBP REST API enhancements

PLA-58003

Changed

Minor

Automatically on

 

Facts in this post come from SAP’s 2H 2026 release notes (latest revision 2 October 2026). Anything labelled Suggested is my recommendation, not SAP’s.

 

1. Proxy: creating proxies and acting as a proxy are now separate permissions

Before: Holding Proxy Management did two jobs. It gave access to the Proxy Management UI to create proxy assignments for the target population. It also let the holder act on behalf of their entire target population for all proxy modules, without an explicit 1:1 proxy assignment. There was no option to restrict proxy access to specific modules in RBP.

Now: The two jobs are separate permissions.

 

Permission

What it does now

Proxy Management

Gives access to the Proxy Management UI to create assignments for the target population.

Proxy Rights (under General User Permission)

Lets administrators act on behalf of their target population for the selected proxy modules. Also used to create group-to-group proxy assignments.

 

When you define a Proxy Rights permission role in Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, you set:

  • Access Population: the users who will act as proxy.
  • Target Population: the users the access population can proxy into.
  • Proxy Modules: all modules or a selected subset, shown in a parent-child hierarchy. Selecting a child module automatically includes its parent.

What happens at release: To avoid disruption, anyone holding Proxy Management at release is automatically granted Proxy Rights with all modules selected. No manual migration step is required. To narrow a role, open it in Manage Permission Roles and update the proxy module selection under the Proxy Rights settings.

Watch-outs from the release note:

  • Selecting the Reporting proxy module or its sub-modules gives the proxy access to all reports. Selecting Performance Management Forms gives access to all Performance Management forms. For more granular control of reports and forms, use the Proxy Management admin tool.
  • To act as a proxy, a user needs either Proxy Rights or an explicit 1:1 proxy assignment created through the Proxy Management tool. When both apply, the explicit 1:1 assignment takes priority.
  • To open the Proxy Management UI, you need the Proxy Management permission in your role.

Why it matters: SAP’s own summary is that you can now give specific administrators access to the proxy management UI without also granting them proxy access.

Suggested: Because the automatic grant is all modules, list everyone who holds Proxy Management and decide who needs all modules, some modules or no proxy rights.

 

2. More MDF objects are secured by default

Before: For these objects, the Access to non-secured objects permission was necessary to view, create and update records. All users who held it could also add and delete objects.

Now: From 2H 2026, eight MDF objects are delivered as secured by default. SAP states that it is not possible to change this setting:

  • Position
  • Position Type
  • Position Right to Return
  • Position Requisition Mapping
  • Position Job Requisition Processing Request
  • Position Requisition Status
  • Company Structure Definition
  • Company Structure UI Configuration

What happens to your existing roles depends on where you started:

 

Your situation

What happens

You had already secured the object

No change

The object was not secured, and the role does not have Access to non-secured objects

No change

The object was not secured, but the role does have Access to non-secured objects

The system grants the role permissions on the object from the new User > Position Management Object Permissions category

 

Two objects from 1H 2026 were also re-documented in this release “for clarity”. They follow the same three-way logic, but the grants go to different categories:

 

Object

Delivered

Where the system grants permissions

Hire Date Correction

1H 2026

Manage Data category: Object-Level Permissions, View, Edit, Import, Export, View Pending Approvals and Review Pending Approvals. The release note says there are no changes to permissions granted in the “Manager User” category.

Fallback Event Reason Configuration

1H 2026

Administrator > Manage Business Configuration category

 

Why SAP made the change: It is part of a general initiative to make all unsecured MDF objects secure by default, so customers make informed decisions on which target groups they provide appropriate permissions to.

Suggested: List the roles that hold Access to non-secured objects and open each in Manage Permission Roles. Review the permissions the system granted under Position Management Object Permissions, Manage Data and Manage Business Configuration. The old permission allowed adding and deleting, so check what the new grants allow and remove anything the role doesn’t need.

 

3. Learning admin roles can now be assigned through RBP

Learning administrator roles can now be assigned in Admin Center > Manage Permission Roles, in addition to the existing standalone Learning role assignment function. In Step 2 (Add Permissions), roles appear as dynamic child permissions under a new permission, Learning Administrator Role Assignment.

How it works:

  • The child permissions are synced from Learning. When Learning admin roles are added or removed in Learning, the child permissions update after the automatically triggered Refresh RBP Model job completes.
  • After you assign the permission to administrators, a daily job, Sync Learning Admin Role Access to Learning, syncs those administrators to Learning. The job runs in delta mode automatically. If you see data inconsistencies, you can trigger a full sync manually in Scheduled Job Manager.
  • If the admin user doesn’t exist in Learning, they are created automatically during role assignment.
  • Assignment and revocation are reflected in Learning within approximately 15 minutes of the sync job completing. Changes are not immediate.
  • Changes to permission groups, such as adding or removing members, are reflected in Learning after the sync job runs.
  • You don’t need to grant Learning admin roles in both RBP and Learning. Managing them through RBP is sufficient.

Rules in the role editor:

  • Selecting only Learning Admin Access Permission, without a role under Learning Administrator Role Assignment, shows an informational message.
  • Selecting Learning Administrator Role Assignment and at least one role selects Learning Admin Access Permission automatically.
  • Unselecting Learning Admin Access Permission also unselects Learning Administrator Role Assignment and resets the dropdown.
  • Selecting Learning Administrator Role Assignment without choosing a role shows an error asking you to provide values for the highlighted fields.

Prerequisite: Learning must be installed in integrated and sealed mode and run version 2H 2026 or higher. If Learning isn’t integrated, is integrated but not sealed, or runs an earlier version, a warning appears in Manage Permission Roles and Learning administrator roles are not shown or available for assignment. SAP points to KBA 3193649 for sealing your Learning instance.

Person mode: If Learning has Person mode enabled, a user may not be removed from the Learning admin role even after the corresponding child permission in RBP is removed. SAP says this is expected, not a bug, and occurs when the same person has another active employment that retains the role.

To verify: In Learning Administration > System Administration > Security > Role Management, open an administrator role and check the Users tab.

 

4. RBP change audit reports now come in two versions

You create the reports as before, in Admin Center > Change Audit Reports > Create Configuration Data Report. The Access Reports tab then shows two versions of each report, for example RBP_GROUP_CHANGE_REPORT and RBP_GROUP_CHANGE_REPORT_V2. V2 has additional data fields, broader audit coverage and faster data availability. It is available for four report types:

 

Report

Major enhancements in V2

RBP Group Change Report

For the Group name field, the original captured only updates to existing names. V2 also covers creation and deletion.

RBP Static Group Membership Change Report

Adds a Display Name column showing the user’s display name.

RBP Role Change Report

Splits Permission into three fields: Permission (standard RBP permissions), Advanced Permission (resource-based permissions that require target criteria during setup) and MDF Permission (Metadata Framework permissions).

 

Splits Role Assignment into Role Assignment Basic Details and Advanced Permission Target Criteria. The new Basic Details field covers permission data blocking information.

 

Splits Group into MDF Permission Basic Target Criteria, MDF Permission Basic Data Blocking and MDF Permission Target Criteria for Position.

 

Adds new fields such as Role Description and RBP-Only.

RBP User Role Change Report

Renames RuleId to Role Assignment ID for clearer identification. The Context 4 Key and Context 4 Value columns, unused in the original report, now show the user’s display name.

(Figure 1:  V2 version of RBP reports)

Prerequisite: Change audit logging must be enabled for your system.

Two behaviors to plan for:

1. V2 may contain more data than the original. It is built on a new audit technology that makes data available faster, so when both reports are generated at the same time, V2 may hold more.

(Figure 2: RBP Group Change Report)

(Figure 3: RBP Role Change Report )

 

2. Audit Log Service can return two sets of records per change. If you access RBP change audit data through SAP Audit Log

Service, the payload may contain one set from the new technology and one from the original. Records from the new technology appear sooner, so a query shortly after a change may return only those, and the original records may arrive later. Check the objectType field in the payload to tell them apart. SAP’s Module-Specific Fields, Attribute Names and Coded Values page explains how to identify records from the new technology.

The release note does not say how long both versions will be offered.

Suggested: Make one permission change, generate both reports and keep the comparison as evidence. Tell anyone who consumes Audit Log Service data that each change may appear twice.

 

5. Hide Story report data for forms that never reached a user’s Inbox

A user with Data Access: Story can view Performance Management data in Story reports for all forms matching the selected form templates and target population. That can include forms that never reached their Inbox and are probably irrelevant to them. SAP’s example is Ask for Feedback requests and replies for forms they weren’t involved in.

The new permission Hide Story Report Data for Forms Never in Inbox (User Permissions > Performance) prevents users from seeing that data. It works together with Data Access: Story and is disabled by default. SAP says it helps ensure data privacy and relevance in Performance Management Story reports.

Requirements:

  • Story reports are enabled.
  • Enable Performance Management Access Permission is selected in the Performance Management Feature Settings admin tool.
  • Users are granted Performance > Data Access: Story.

Suggested: Review who holds Data Access: Story and decide whether they should see data for forms that never reached their Inbox. If not, grant the new permission.

 

6. REST API enhancements

  • POST /assignments now returns an id field for the created assignment, so you no longer need a follow-up GET request. Previously it returned only a 201 Created status code.
  • POST /roles and PUT /roles now support an externalCode field for MDF permissions in both requests and responses. For requests involving MDF permissions, you must provide either the MDF entity’s externalCode or its resourceId. The external code applies only to MDF permissions (resource type MDF_OBJECT), not to other resource-based permissions.

SAP will update the API documentation on SAP Business Accelerator Hub (SAP SuccessFactors Role-Based Permission Management API) on the Valid as Of date, 13 November 2026.

Sample Code 
"resources": [
    {
      "resourceId": 111,
      "externalCode": "obj4qaBEDataSource", //External code of the MDF resource. Only applicable when resourceType is MDF_OBJECT.
      "resourceType": "MDF_OBJECT",
      "selectedActions": [
        {
          "name": "VIEW_HISTORY"
        } ...

Suggested: If you manage roles or assignments through scripts or integrations, check that MDF permission requests supply externalCode or resourceId. You can also use the returned assignment id instead of a follow-up GET.

 

Pre-release checklist (suggested)

 

#

Action

Related change

1

List everyone holding Proxy Management. They will receive Proxy Rights for all modules. Decide who should be narrowed.

Proxy

2

Identify roles holding Access to non-secured objects and review the grants the system added (Position Management Object Permissions, Manage Data, Manage Business Configuration).

MDF

3

Confirm Learning is integrated, sealed and on 2H 2026 or higher. Agree whether RBP becomes the single place to manage Learning admins.

Learning

4

Run the original and V2 reports after one test change. Decide which version is your evidence of record.

Audit

5

Tell consumers of Audit Log Service data about duplicate record sets and the objectType field.

Audit

6

Decide whether to grant Hide Story Report Data for Forms Never in Inbox, and to whom.

Story

7

Check integrations that call POST /assignments or POST/PUT /roles.

API

8

Update control descriptions and screenshots in your audit documentation.

Audit

 

Suggested tests

 

Test

What to confirm

Grant Proxy Management only (no Proxy Rights, no 1:1 assignment) to a test user

User can open the Proxy Management UI but cannot act as proxy

Define a Proxy Rights role with one child module

Proxy can act in that module and its parent. Check the Reporting and Performance Management Forms behavior.

Open a role that held Access to non-secured objects

New grants appear under Position Management Object Permissions, and you can explain each one

Assign a Learning admin role through RBP

Admin appears in Learning (Role Management > Users tab) about 15 minutes after the sync job completes

Change an MDF permission and a role assignment, then run both reports

The change appears in the V2 split fields (MDF Permission, Role Assignment Basic Details, Advanced Permission Target Criteria)

Make one change and query Audit Log Service twice, shortly after and later

Count the record sets and use objectType to separate new from original records

Grant the Story hiding permission to a test user

Data for forms never in their Inbox no longer appears in Story reports

Call POST /assignments

Response includes id

Create or update a role with an MDF permission via POST/PUT /roles

Request accepts externalCode or resourceId, and the response includes externalCode

 

Closing thought

Four of these changes tighten control or evidence. Proxy Rights separates managing proxies from being one, the MDF change secures more objects, V2 gives finer audit fields, and the Story permission lets you hide data for forms users never received. The Learning change centralizes administration in RBP, and the API change makes automation easier.

Two changes also act on your roles automatically: the Proxy Rights grant and the Position Management grants. SAP designed them to avoid disruption, so they carry over the access your roles already had. That is our reading, not SAP’s, but it is why both deserve a review before 13 November.

Disclaimer: Test every change in your preview environment before it reaches production, and validate it against your own role and permission design. SAP can change its release notes at any time, and this post reflects them as last revised on 2 October 2026. Always check the SAP SuccessFactors What’s New Viewer for the latest updates.
